neighbours.label: the word inside a terse verbless fragment that follows a full sentence in casual writing (Badly. Or a friend. Yep.)
fire: She finally finished the marathon. Slowly. But she finished.
He forgot their anniversary again. Or his wife's birthday. Or both.
Did the new menu work out? Nope. Not even close.
I love strong tea in the morning. Lots of it. With honey.
The repairs will be done by spring. Maybe. If we are lucky.
They lost the final in the last minute. Painfully. Again.
Is the movie worth seeing? Absolutely. Bring tissues.
Nobody had cleaned the kitchen for weeks. Or the bathroom. Gross.
quiet: She finally finished the marathon slowly, but she did finish it in the end.
He forgot their anniversary again, and he also forgot his wife's birthday.
Did the new menu work out? The owner says sales have not improved at all.
I love drinking a lot of strong tea with honey in the morning.
The repairs will probably be done by spring if the weather is good.
They lost the final in the last minute, which was painful for the fans again.
Is the movie worth seeing? My friends said it was sad but very good.
Nobody had cleaned the kitchen or the bathroom for several weeks.

notes: Top examples: ' Yep', 'Or a friend', 'Bad-ly', 'Lots of it', 'Or ever'. The + pole is the '.' before such a fragment (promotes Or/Especially/Which). Probes 0.27-1.03 on fragments, 0.05-0.08 on the same content as one sentence.
